summary: A unit test runs a small piece of code with known inputs and checks the result. Node has a built-in assert module, and check() here runs each test and prints PASS or FAIL.
notes: assert.strictEqual(actual, expected) throws an AssertionError if actual !== expected. check() catches it and prints FAIL.
assert.throws(() => letterGrade(101), RangeError) needs an arrow function, so the code runs inside assert.throws where the error can be caught.
Node also has node:test with test() blocks and a node --test command. Its report prints timings that change on every run.
pitfall: Writing assert.throws(letterGrade(101), RangeError) calls letterGrade right away, so the RangeError is thrown before assert.throws can catch it and the test crashes. Wrap the call in () => ...
contrast: Python ships unittest with test classes, and Java projects add JUnit. Node ships both an assert module and a node:test runner, so no install is needed.
